page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.large is a compute-oriented virtual server instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 vCPUs backed by 1 physical core with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 2.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The CPU topology incorporates a 35 MB L3 cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache, with support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES cryptography, and FMA. The instance runs on a KVM hypervisor and offers a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It does not include local disk storage or integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements indicate modest baseline performance across computational and memory operations. Single-core stress-ng tests record a score of 1098.29, while multi-core execution achieves 1457.69. Uncached memory bandwidth testing registers 10.26 GB/sec for large-block reads and 9.37 GB/sec for large-block writes. Application-level metrics show Redis SET throughput of 1.43 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 1.77 GB/sec. In small-scale artificial intelligence benchmarks using a 135M parameter model, the instance yields 123.4 tokens per second during prompt processing and 37.46 tokens per second during text generation.

The 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with dedicated CPU allocation provides consistent access to processing capacity without CPU credit throttling. However, the limited 2.0 GB memory allocation represents a primary constraint, restricting concurrency and preventing the execution of memory-heavy workloads. Given the lack of bundled local storage and limited RAM headroom, the ecs.ic5.large instance is best suited for lightweight microservices, basic API proxies, entry-level web serving, and minor computational background tasks.
